mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 6 Series 635csi engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A used BMW 635csi M30 engine typically costs £1,200-£3,500 depending on mileage, condition and specification (early L-Jetronic vs later Motronic). A reconditioned unit ranges from £2,500-£5,200, while a fully rebuilt engine with warranty sits at £4,000-£7,000. Specialist fitting adds approximately £1,000-£1,600 in labour (14-20 hours at £65-£85/hr). Main dealer fitting costs 40-60% more.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain wear in a BMW 635csi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M30's timing chain is generally robust, but the tensioner can wear over time. The classic symptom is a rattling noise from the front of the engine on cold start that partially disappears as the engine warms up. In more advanced cases, the chain can become slack, affecting valve timing and causing power loss or rough running.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 6 Series 635csi?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on the car's condition and value. An E24 635csi typically holds £8,000-£30,000+ value depending on condition, mileage and specification. A rebuilt M30 engine at £4,000-£7,000 is typically justifiable if the car is otherwise sound and rust-free. However, if the car has significant body rot or other major issues, evaluate the total repair cost against the vehicle's value.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the M30B34 and M30B35 engines in the BMW 635csi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M30B34 was fitted from 1984-1987 and used Bosch Motronic 1.0 fuel injection, producing 218hp (non-cat) or 185hp (with catalyst). The M30B35 was fitted from 1987-1989 and used the more advanced Bosch Motronic 1.3, producing 211hp. The B35 has larger intake valves, a more breathable intake and a different cam profile.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 6 Series 635csi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 635csi engine replacement takes 4-8 days from booking to collection, depending on parts availability and workshop workload. The M30 is an older engine, so sourcing a quality rebuilt or reconditioned unit may take 3-5 days. Supply and fit through our network typically completes within 5-8 working days.

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a BMW 635csi replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Rebuilt and reconditioned M30 engines typically include full parts and labour cover; used engines usually carry a 3-6 month warranty depending on the supplier. Always confirm that the timing chain components are covered under the warranty terms.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 6 Series 635csi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 635csi was the flagship model of the first-generation E24 6 Series, launched in 1978 as the most powerful and best-equipped variant in the range. Powered exclusively by the legendary M30 inline-six engine family, the 635csi represented the pinnacle of BMW's grand touring engineering for over a decade - until the arrival of the M635csi in 1984. The E24 635csi was produced from 1978 to 1989.

milestones.description: M30B35 (3.5L / 3,453cc), 218hp - E24 635csi launched as the flagship 6 Series model, featuring Bosch L-Jetronic fuel injection
M30B35 (3.5L / 3,430cc), 218hp - Displacement reduced slightly; technical updates to engine management
M30B34 (3.4L / 3,430cc), 218hp - Updated with Bosch Motronic 1.0 fuel injection; catalytic converter optional (185hp with cat)
M30B34 (3.4L / 3,430cc), 211hp - Catalytic converter fitted as standard; power output 211hp
1989 - M30B35 (3.4L / 3,430cc), 208hp - Final two model years; improved engine management with Bosch Motronic 1.3

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 6 Series 635csi is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 6 Series 635csi Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW 635csi's M30 engine is legendary for its robust, "bulletproof" design - a cast-iron block, aluminium cylinder head, single overhead cam and two valves per cylinder. However, age and mileage have exposed several well-documented weak points. The M30 is famously durable, with many examples exceeding 200,000 miles on original internals, but cooling system neglect, fuel injection issues, and timing chain wear are the primary drivers of replacement demand. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain & Tensioner Wear - The High-Mileage Risk
problems.rootCause: The M30's timing chain is generally robust and chain jump is rare unless the tensioner fails. However, the spring in the tensioner weakens over time, and piston or chain rail wear can cause a loose or slack chain. A rattling noise on cold start that partially goes away as the engine warms up is the classic warning sign.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace tensioner piston and spring; inspect chain rail
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if caught early; rattle on start-up only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full timing chain kit, guides, tensioners; cam timing
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if chain has stretched or guides are worn
Only if chain has jumped or caused catastrophic damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: An E24 635csi typically holds £8,000-£30,000+ value depending on condition, mileage and specification. Timing chain replacement at specialist rates (£1,500-£2,500) is a justifiable investment on most examples. Full engine replacement is viable on higher-value cars but should be carefully evaluated against the vehicle's overall condition.
problems.recommendation: Address timing chain rattle promptly - it's far cheaper to replace the tensioner or chain than to rebuild an engine after a jumped chain. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the tensioner inspected immediately.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M30B34 BMW 6 Series 635csi engine prices

problems.h4: Cooling System Neglect - The Overheat Risk
problems.rootCause: The M30's cooling system is robust but age takes its toll. The water pump and thermostat will eventually fail. Failure to change coolant and use the correct type results in aluminium oxidation forming inside the cylinder-head coolant passages, causing hot running. A seized fan coupling is another common issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace water pump, thermostat, coolant flush

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if fan is seized or not engaging properly
Only if overheating has caused head gasket or head damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: These repairs are all well within the value of any 635csi. The water pump is the most critical - failure can lead to overheating and cylinder head damage far exceeding the cost of preventative replacement.
problems.recommendation: Replace the water pump, thermostat and fan coupling preventatively every 60k-80k miles. Use the correct BMW-spec coolant and change it every two years. This is the single most effective way to avoid catastrophic overheating on the M30.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M30B35 BMW 6 Series 635csi engine prices

problems.h4: Fuel Injection & Idle Issues - L-Jetronic vs Motronic
problems.rootCause: Early 635csi models use Bosch L-Jetronic injection, while later models use Motronic 1.0 or 1.3. Common issues include rough idle, hesitation just off idle, and hot-start problems. The cold start injector can leak, causing difficult hot starting. Fuel relays should be the first check if the injection system stops working.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable if leaking or causing hot-start issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full diagnostic; check relays, sensors, injectors
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if idle or driveability issues persist
Only if injection failure has caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Fuel injection repairs are well within the value of any 635csi. Specialist diagnosis is the most cost-effective approach - M30 injection systems are well-understood by classic BMW specialists.
problems.recommendation: Start with the basics - check fuel relays, replace the fuel filter annually, and have the injection system professionally diagnosed if you experience rough idle or hesitation. A simple sensor or relay replacement is often all that's needed.
